Filling a bottle by area, not height

Josh asked how to write the bottle chart so the amount is the filled area of the bottle instead of the fill's height. Today 75% fills the bottle to 75% of its height, which holds 88% of its area. Filling by area means inverting the silhouette's cumulative area. That inverse is a coordinate transform, the same idea as d3.scaleRadial and the proposed Coord.clock({ radius: "area" }).

Recommendation: one new coord, Coord.region(ref("glass"), { y: "area" }). It maps a layer's box onto another node's region (its alpha, as drawn), so equal heights in the layer are equal areas in the bottle. The liquid stays rect({ h: "amount" }). Stacked liquids, equal-area waffles and fill animations then need no new mark or channel.

Runner-up: a data helper fillLevel(outline, { measure: "area" }) in derive. It is cheaper, but it breaks stacking: the bands' heights stop being amounts.

Every picture is a real GoFish render from stories/proposals/BottleArea.stories.tsx. None of the proposed APIs exist yet, so each render draws what the proposal would produce, using today's primitives with fill levels computed in JS from the PNG's alpha channel. Renders marked emulated are these. Precedent pictures are labeled sketches.

How far apart height and area are

Height encoding (today's story)

Area encoding emulated

Measured from the alpha channel of wilsonblanco.png (157 × 650 px), the fill level as a share of the bottle's height:

amount height area volume
30% 0.30 0.26 0.24
42% 0.42 0.35 0.33
60% 0.60 0.49 0.45
75% 0.75 0.61 0.55
90% 0.90 0.80 0.66

The top 30% of the height, the neck and shoulder, holds 15% of the area and 7% of the volume. So height encoding overstates every amount, most near the top. In a cone (a martini glass) area grows with the square of the level, so 50% by area sits at 71% of the depth.

Precedent

No visualization library found fills a picture by area. The idea exists in cartography, transport maps and tank gauging, and in GoFish's own area decisions.

PiCCL

Shi et al., VIS 2025. Source of the bottle chart. Binds a picture's height. 

new PICCL.Picture({ url: "bottle.png" }).mapValue("height", "amount");

echarts-liquidfill

Liquid gauge. The level is a share of the box height, even in a circle. 

series: [{ type: "liquidFill", data: [0.25], shape: "path://M..." }];
// source: waterLevel = radiusY - value * radiusY * 2 (share of box height)

Vega-Lite, Observable Plot

No support. A bar is clipped to an SVG clip path. Height encoding by construction. 

// No fill-by-area. The usual hack clips a bar to an SVG <clipPath>.
Plot.barY(data, { y: "amount" }); // then style: clip-path: url(#bottle)

Figma, Illustrator

Clipping mask: the bottom shape of a group clips the rest. No data. GoFish's atop. 

Select shapes, then "Use as mask"

Bertin, d3.scaleRadial

Area = Q, radius grows with √Q (Bertin p. 357–358). Equal rings have equal area. 

const r = d3.scaleRadial().domain([0, max]).range([0, R]); // area linear in data

GoFish today and in flight

circle({ area }) (merged, #1323); Coord.clock({ radius: "area" }) (proposed). Both keep data linear in a measure. 

circle({ area: "count" }); // #972, merged in #1323
chart(data, { coord: Coord.clock({ radius: "area" }) }); // proposed (scale transforms)

Lambert equal-area (1772)

y = sin(latitude): the sphere's cumulative band area, inverted. Equal steps in y are equal areas.

Knothe–Rosenblatt map

Knothe 1957, Rosenblatt 1952. Unit square onto a region by inverse cumulative measure, one axis then the other. Constant area scaling.

Tank strapping tables

Tank calibration: a table from dipstick level to volume for a tank's shape. Level and volume are different numbers.

level volume
0.25 0.20
0.50 0.50
0.75 0.80

Horizontal cylinder; the 0.25 row is the circular segment's share, 0.196.

Perception literature

Cleveland and McGill 1984: length beats area. Stevens: perceived area grows about as area0.7.

Area encoding is not automatically more accurate. It makes the drawn liquid agree with the data, while height encoding makes the level agree. That is a choice for the author, so neither should be a hidden default.

ISOTYPE

Haroz, Kosara and Franconeri, CHI 2015. Pictographs do not hurt accuracy and help memory.

Supports pictorial fills. The equal-area waffle below is an isotype inside a silhouette.

Tufte's lie factor

1983. Scaling a picture in 2D for 1D data inflates the effect.

The reverse case: a 1D level in a 2D container misstates the 2D amount.

Recommended: Coord.region

Coord.region(shape, { y }) maps its layer's box onto shape's region. Height in the layer runs along the region by the chosen measure; width runs across the region at each level. With y: "area", every rect in the layer has screen area proportional to its data area. The bottle stays outside the coord, so it is not warped.

Diff tint on the right column:added or changed removed (left column)

1. The bottle row

The only change is a coord layer around the liquid. The guide line now aligns to the liquid's top instead of reading y: "amount" itself, because outside the coord a height is a length, not an area.

Today

chart(data, { axes: false })
  .flow(spread({ by: "category", dir: "x", spacing: 20, axes: { x: false } }))
  .mark(
    layer([
      atop({ blendMode: "color" }, [
        image({ href: bottlePng, h: v(100), filter: Filter.grayscale }),
        rect({ h: "amount", w: 175, fill: "#00ff00" }),
      ]).name("bottle"),
      rect({ h: 1, fill: "#666", w: 175, y: "amount" }).name("line"),
      text({ fontSize: 35, fill: "#666", text: (d) => `${d.amount}%` }).name(
        "label"
      ),
    ]).relate(({ line, label, bottle }) => [
      Constraint.align({ x: "start" }, [bottle, line]),
      Constraint.distribute({ dir: "y", spacing: 0 }, [line, label]),
      Constraint.align({ x: "end" }, [label, line]),
    ])
  )
  .render(container, {});

Proposed emulated

chart(data, { axes: false })
  .flow(spread({ by: "category", dir: "x", spacing: 20, axes: { x: false } }))

      Constraint.align({ y: "end" }, [liquid, line]),

2. Stacked liquids: "What's in a bottle of wine"

The data of the Forward Syntax/Cut story, which says "by volume" but slices by height. The bands are a plain stack of amounts; the coord inverts the cumulative sums once, so CanSum survives and the data stays in amounts.

Today (stack, clipped by atop) emulated 

atop({ blendMode: "multiply" }, [
  image({ href: bottlePng, h: 520, filter: Filter.grayscale }).name("glass"),
  chart(wine)
    .flow(stack({ dir: "y" }))
    .mark(rect({ h: "amount", fill: "category" })),
]).render(container, {});

Proposed emulated

atop({ blendMode: "multiply" }, [
  image({ href: bottlePng, h: 520, filter: Filter.grayscale }).name("glass"),
  chart(wine, { coord: Coord.region(ref("glass"), { y: "area" }) })
    .flow(stack({ dir: "y" }))
    .mark(rect({ h: "amount", fill: "category" })),
]).render(container, {});
Python 
atop(
    [
        image(href=BOTTLE_PNG, h=520, filter=Filter.grayscale).name("glass"),
        chart(WINE, coord=Coord.region(ref("glass"), y="area"))
        .flow(stack(dir="y"))
        .mark(rect(h="amount", fill="category")),
    ],
    blend_mode="multiply",
).render(container, {})

Labels in these renders are placed by hand. In the proposal they would be .label() on the bands or aligned to them, as in example 1.

3. Hard example: martini glasses

The container is the bowl, not the picture: the stem is solid glass. So the region is a shape the user names, the bowl's outline, not the whole picture. In a cone, area grows with the square of the level.

{ y: "length" } (today's picture) emulated 

// The container is the bowl, not the picture: the stem is solid glass.
// polygon({ w, h, d }) is the unit-box outline from PR #1340.
chart(cocktails, { axes: false })
  .flow(spread({ by: "drink", dir: "x", spacing: 70 }))
  .mark(
    layer([
      polygon({
        w: 150,
        h: v(100),
        d: "M0 1 L1 1 L.5 0 Z",
        fill: "none",
        stroke: "#555",
      }).name("bowl"),
      layer({ coord: Coord.region(ref("bowl"), { y: "length" }) }, [
        rect({ h: "full", fill: "#c8d84a" }),
      ]),
      rect({ w: 3, h: 90, fill: "#555" }).name("stem"),
    ]).relate(({ bowl, stem }) => [
      Constraint.distribute({ dir: "y", spacing: 0 }, [stem, bowl]),
      Constraint.align({ x: "middle" }, [stem, bowl]),
    ])
  )
  .render(container, {});

4. Hard example: an equal-area waffle in the bottle

A 10 × 10 grid laid out in the coord. With area, every cell has the same area, so 60 green cells are 60% of the bottle; the neck's cells are tall and thin. Only a 2D map can draw this; a level alone cannot.

{ y: "length" } emulated 

// Rows of equal height: the cells in the neck are small.
layer([
  image({ href: bottlePng, h: 520, opacity: 0.35 }).name("glass"),
  chart(cells, { coord: Coord.region(ref("glass"), { y: "length" }) })
    .flow(stack({ by: "row", dir: "y" }), stack({ by: "col", dir: "x" }))
    .mark(
      rect({ fill: (d) => (d.k < 60 ? "#2f9e44" : "#d9d9d9"), stroke: "white" })
    ),
]).render(container, {});

{ y: "area" } emulated 

// 100 cells of equal area: the coord is a 2D map, not only a level.
layer([
  image({ href: bottlePng, h: 520, opacity: 0.35 }).name("glass"),
  chart(cells, { coord: Coord.region(ref("glass"), { y: "area" }) })
    .flow(stack({ by: "row", dir: "y" }), stack({ by: "col", dir: "x" }))
    .mark(
      rect({ fill: (d) => (d.k < 60 ? "#2f9e44" : "#d9d9d9"), stroke: "white" })
    ),
]).render(container, {});

The map, and how it composes

For a point (u, v) in the unit square, take the level y = A⁻¹(u · A_total), where A is the cumulative area, and go v of the way across the silhouette at that level. The area scaling is w(y) · dy/du = A_total, a constant. Where a level crosses the silhouette more than once (the legs of a figure, a ring), v runs across the spans left to right and the scaling stays constant.

  • Stacking. A plain stack in the coord. This is the "fixed by geometry" nonlinearity already decided for area circles: data stays linear in a measure, so CanSum and the origin survive.
  • Guide lines and labels. Anything at the level lives in the coord or aligns to a node in it.
  • Animation. Tweening h from 0 raises the liquid at a constant pour rate: fast in the body, slow in the neck.
  • Glyphs. A circle or text in the coord is a glyph and is not warped (the rule from #1323). A rect's area is warped, which is the point.
  • Other coords. A region coord inside a polar or geo layer needs coords to nest. Unverified today; a cost, not a design change.
  • What "full" means. The coord warps its frame, the named node's box, and owns no data domain. So image({ h: v(100) }) still says 100 is a full bottle, as today.
  • Desugaring. A coord is a point map, so no node kind is added. What is new is the parameter: another node's region, read after that node is laid out (and, for a raster, after its pixels load).

Overlap check. With y: "length", a full-width rect in the coord draws the same picture as today's atop clip: a small exact overlap; atop keeps paint and blending. An area-measured cut is cut slices placed in this coord, so cut gets no measure option. Coord.clock({ radius: "area" }) is the same kernel swept along rings instead of rows: for a disk, Coord.region gives a round flask's horizontal slices and the clock gives a pie's rings. They should share one implementation. circle({ area }) sizes a mark's own glyph and does not overlap.

Other approaches

AData helper in derive

Runner-up. The user computes the level; the picture is today's code with "level" for "amount". Renders the same as example 1. 

// The data side cannot read an image, so the outline is a vector path.
const level = fillLevel(BOTTLE_D, { measure: "area" }); // share -> share of height

chart(data, { axes: false })
  .flow(
    derive((rows) =>
      rows.map((d) => ({ ...d, level: 100 * level(d.amount / 100) }))
    ),
    spread({ by: "category", dir: "x", spacing: 20, axes: { x: false } })
  )
  .mark(
    layer([
      atop({ blendMode: "color" }, [
        image({ href: bottlePng, h: v(100), filter: Filter.grayscale }),
        rect({ h: "level", w: 175, fill: "#00ff00" }),
      ]).name("bottle"),
      rect({ h: 1, fill: "#666", w: 175, y: "level" }).name("line"),
      text({ fontSize: 35, fill: "#666", text: (d) => `${d.amount}%` }).name(
        "label"
      ),
    ]).relate(({ line, label, bottle }) => [
      Constraint.align({ x: "start" }, [bottle, line]),
      Constraint.distribute({ dir: "y", spacing: 0 }, [line, label]),
      Constraint.align({ x: "end" }, [label, line]),
    ])
  )
  .render(container, {});
Python 
level = fill_level(BOTTLE_D, measure="area")

chart(DATA, axes=False).flow(
    derive(lambda rows: [{**d, "level": 100 * level(d["amount"] / 100)} for d in rows]),
    spread(by="category", dir="x", spacing=20, axes={"x": False}),
).mark(
    BOTTLE_MARK
)  # today's mark, with "level" in place of "amount" for h and y

Stacked, the hard case:

// Stacked: each band's height depends on everything below it, so the user
// sums, inverts, then takes differences. The bands' h no longer add up as amounts.
const level = fillLevel(BOTTLE_D, { measure: "area" });
let below = 0;
const bands = wine.map((d) => {
  const lo = level(below / 100);
  below += d.amount;
  return { ...d, h: 100 * (level(below / 100) - lo) };
});
chart(bands)
  .flow(stack({ dir: "y" }))
  .mark(rect({ h: "h", fill: "category" }));

Each band's h depends on every band below it, so it is not an amount and changes with order. Needs a vector outline, since data runs before images load. Cannot draw the waffle.

BA channel of the container

Like circle({ area }), but on the bottle.

// The fill is a channel of the container mark, as area is a channel of circle.
image({
  href: bottlePng,
  h: v(100),
  liquid: { amount: "amount", measure: "area", fill: "#00ff00" },
});
Python 
image(
    href=BOTTLE_PNG,
    h=datum(100),
    liquid={"amount": "amount", "measure": "area", "fill": "#00ff00"},
)

The wall: circle({ area }) sizes the circle's own geometry. The level depends on a different shape. Putting the channel on the container makes the liquid part of one mark kind, so stacking, labels, color by field and waffles each need another option. Large partial overlap with atop + rect and with cut. Not recommended.

DClip plus a solved constraint

The liquid is the bottle intersected with a rect whose height a constraint solves. 

layer([
  image({ href: bottlePng, h: v(100) }).name("glass"),
  intersect([ref("glass").hidden(), rect({ fill: "#00ff00" })]).name("liquid"),
]).relate(({ glass, liquid }) => [
  Constraint.share({ measure: "area", value: "amount", whole: 100 }, [
    liquid,
    glass,
  ]),
]);
Python 
layer(
    [
        image(href=BOTTLE_PNG, h=datum(100)).name("glass"),
        intersect([ref("glass").hidden(), rect(fill="#00ff00")]).name("liquid"),
    ]
).relate(
    lambda glass, liquid: [
        Constraint.share([liquid, glass], measure="area", value="amount", whole=100),
    ]
)

C restricted to one rect, solved by root finding: a degenerate case of C. Needs a new nonlinear constraint that reads painted area. Stacks need chained constraints; no waffle.

Measure grid

The option value picks what "how full" means. length reproduces today; volume weights each row by its width squared, as for a solid of revolution. The scale-transforms rule "embedding decides the invariant" (a 2D mark keeps a 2D measure) argues for area; a real bottle holds volume, and tank tables exist because people need it.

length

Level = share of the height. Today's picture.

Coord.region(ref("glass"), { y: "length" });

area recommended

Filled area = share of the silhouette's area.

Coord.region(ref("glass"), { y: "area" });

volume open

Filled volume of the solid of revolution = share.

Coord.region(ref("glass"), { y: "volume" });

Where the silhouette comes from

Source How the profile is read Cost
A vector outline: polygon({ points }), or polygon({ w, h, d }) from #1340 Exactly, from the polygon or path. The user needs an outline that matches the picture.
A raster image's alpha Decode the image and count opaque pixels per row (what the prototype did offline, at alpha > 128). Layout waits for the image; the threshold is a choice. Python renders through JS, so it is not a separate problem.

The martini shows the container is often not the picture's silhouette, so the region argument is any node the user names, spelled with ref. A raster read is then one way a node exposes its region, not an option of the coord.

Trade-offs

A. derive helper B. container channel C. Coord.region D. solved clip
Single fill yes yes yes yes
Stacked liquids keep amounts (CanSum) no needs more options yes chained constraints
Equal-area waffle no no yes no
Pour-rate animation per-frame recompute maybe yes re-solve
Raster silhouette no yes yes yes
Container ≠ picture (martini) yes no yes yes
New concepts one helper a channel kind one coord; a coord that reads a ref a nonlinear constraint
Overlap none (the escape hatch) large, partial exact, with atop and cut degenerate case of C

Recommendation

C, Coord.region(ref(name), { y: "length" | "area" }).

  • It desugars into the core: a coord is a point map, and liquids, stacks and waffles are existing marks and operators. Only the coord's parameter is new (principles, "Why keep the core small").
  • One concept, one operator: single fills, stacked fills, waffles and area-measured cuts are one idea, a measure-preserving map onto a region. B and D each cover one case. Overlaps with atop and cut are exact compositions (api-design, "Overlap is fine at the edges").
  • Meaning stays on the data: amounts stay amounts, matching the "fixed by geometry" rule already decided for circle({ area }) and Coord.clock({ radius: "area" }).
  • Names match precedent: "region" is GoFish's word for a node's alpha (#1267); the option mirrors radius: "area".
  • A default is sugar: y: "length" reproduces today; "area" is a written choice.
  • Same shape in Python: Coord.region(ref("glass"), y="area").

Runner-up, A. Pick it if a coord that reads a sibling needs a second layout pass the engine cannot afford, or if single bottles are the only real use. It is worth documenting anyway as the escape hatch.

What would change the pick. If coords cannot read another node's geometry, C's parameter becomes a literal outline (Coord.region(Shape.path(d))) and loses rasters. If volume is in scope, C still holds with a third value, and "embedding decides the invariant" needs a vessel exception.

Decisions for Josh

  1. Is filling a silhouette by area a coord (C) or a data helper (A)?
  2. Name: Coord.region, Coord.inside, or Coord.within?
  3. Spell the measure { y: "area" }, mirroring Coord.clock({ radius: "area" }), with default "length"?
  4. Is y: "volume" (solid of revolution) in scope?
  5. May a coord's parameter be a ref to a sibling, laid out first, or only a literal outline?
  6. Does a raster image's alpha count as a region for layout, or must the user give a vector outline?
  7. Should Coord.region and Coord.clock({ radius: "area" }) be documented as one idea (inverse cumulative measure along a sweep) now, or later?
  8. cut stays length-only, and an area cut is a cut in a region coord. Agreed?
  9. Switch the Bottle gallery story to area once this exists, and fix the Cut story's "by volume" comment now?

Found along the way

  • The Cut story says "by volume" but slices by height: water and grape juice (82%) take 82% of the height, which holds about 91% of the area.
  • echarts-liquidfill fills by height even in its default circle.
